Title: Veyil
Body (HTML):
Every household keeps a katta pai by the door, the one grabbed without thinking, on the way out for a market run in the sun.

Veyil carries that same instinct into a hand bag people would actually want seen: the same brightness, the same readiness, made to be carried in the open sun. A circle cut clean through leather, the weave burning through the opening.

Title: Nizhal
Body (HTML):
There’s a particular kind of afternoon, too warm to be outside, quiet enough that the tiles hold the light in patches. Nizhal is that pause.

A shoulder bag built for the hours when the sun has moved off you and everything slows down — structured, close, unhurried, the shape of an afternoon slow.

Title: Maalai
Body (HTML):
A paai, laid out flat, holds an entire gathering, from food and conversation to people settling in around it.

Maalai carries that same instinct into a tote: beige and black striped, wide and unfussy, made to hold whatever a day brings into it. Not only evenings, but just everything.

Title: Vizha — Long Clutch
Body (HTML):
Some nights aren’t ordinary, and the bag shouldn’t be either. Vizha is the colour saved for those: gem-toned, worn only when there’s a reason — a wedding, a festival, a night worth dressing for.

One length of paai runs unbroken across the back, over the flap and down the front — a single piece, folded rather than joined.

Title: Vizha — Half Moon
Body (HTML):
Some colours are kept back. They are not for the floor or the afternoon; they come out of the cupboard for weddings, for temple nights, for the days a house fills up.

The weave rises on both sides of a leather handle and meets at the top: a mat folded once, and carried by the fold.
